properties.title: Learning Continuous Patient Trajectories from Electronic Health Records

membership.reason: EHRFlow models continuously evolving latent patient state trajectories from irregular longitudinal EHR histories via history-conditioned multi-marginal flow matching.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L1 predictive continuous-time latent EHR trajectory world model (WT_EHR, BP_FORECAST).

properties.backbone: Observation encoder E_psi + history encoder + history-conditioned multi-marginal flow-matching vector field (GP-CFM / MMFM) + decoder D_phi

properties.flow: Irregular EHR history H_{i,a} + anchor state z_{i,a} -> continuous ODE integration of learned vector field over horizon Delta -> decoded future EHR events/measurements

properties.purpose: Longitudinal patient trajectory forecasting across arbitrary horizons from sparse, irregular EHRs.
properties.environment: Retrospective CPRD and external AMC-EHR (>1M patients) + synthetic benchmarks

assertions.rationale: Explicit calendar timestamps tau_{i,j} and forecast horizon Delta = tau_{s1} - tau_{s0}.
Continuous-time vector field over normalized flow time accommodates sparse, irregularly sampled EHR visits.
Observation encoder E_psi(x_{i,j}) mapping mixed-type clinical vectors to R^{d_z}.
Continuous latent patient state z evolving along flow-matching ODE trajectories.
Vector field explicitly conditioned on encoded preceding patient history H_{i,a}.
Continuous-time neural vector field integrated from anchor state to arbitrary horizon Delta.
Learned multi-marginal flow-matching vector field (GP-CFM and MMFM variants).
Decoder D_phi maps predicted latent states back to continuous and discrete EHR observations.

Evaluates future clinical-code and latent-state trajectory forecasting across 6 synthetic benchmarks (Table 1) and >1M real-world patients in CPRD (0.638 GP-CFM / 0.621 MMFM top-5 accuracy) and external AMC-EHR (0.283 / 0.302; Table 2, p. 7), outperforming autoregressive and history-independent flow-matching baselines (q < 0.05), plus direct-vs-rollout consistency (93-94% top-5 overlap) and unseen-horizon forecasting.
Individual patient trajectory forecasting from longitudinal EHRs.
Horizon-averaged top-5 clinical-code accuracy and latent-state recovery across 6 synthetic benchmarks and >1M-patient CPRD/AMC-EHR.
Controlled synthetic antihypertensive intervention simulation with CFG recovers known BP effect within 0.07-2.07 mmHg (proof of concept).
Independent external validation on AMC-EHR cohort in addition to UK CPRD primary-care records.
Synthetic training/evaluation takes 0.18-0.76 hours vs 10.02-56.94 hours for autoregressive baselines.
State evolution computed in continuous latent space z in R^{d_z}.

evidence_fragments.content: We introduceEHRFlow, a multi-marginal flow-matching framework that conditions on encoded patient history, thereby allowing future dynamics to depend on the patient’s prior clinical trajectory. Our proposed framework accommodates irregular observation times and supports forecasting at arbitrary horizons. Across controlled synthetic benchmarks,EHRFlowimproves clinical-code forecasting and latent-state recovery. On real-world clinical datasets comprising more than one million patients, including an independent external validation cohort,EHRFlowimproves horizon-averaged top-5 clinical-code accuracy over autoregressive and history-independent flowmatching baselines.

EHRFlowbuilds on these multi-observation path constructions by explicitly conditioning the vector field on the patient history available at the forecast anchor. Its latent formulation supports forecasts of both continuous and discrete clinical tokens at arbitrary horizons. Future observations supervise the training path, while preceding observations provide inference-time context (see Figure 2).

[paraphrase (visual p.7)] Table 1 & Table 2 (p. 7): Horizon-averaged top-5 clinical-code accuracy across 6 synthetic benchmarks (Table 1; EHRFlow outperforms all baselines, q < 10^-5) and real-world CPRD (EHRFlow GP-CFM 0.638±0.009, MMFM 0.621±0.021 vs GP-CFM 0.554, MMFM 0.548, Decoder-only 0.368, Encoder-decoder 0.335) and external AMC-EHR (EHRFlow GP-CFM 0.283±0.013, MMFM 0.302±0.016 vs GP-CFM 0.275, MMFM 0.279, Decoder-only 0.259, Encoder-decoder 0.232; q < 0.05).

GuidedEHRFlowapproximates the simulator-defined effect with an average error of 0.07–2.07 mmHg across both models and evaluation settings, equivalent to a relative error of 0.3%–10.1% (Table 4). These results suggest that the learned latent trajectories can preserve clinically meaningful changes in individual physiological variables, as demonstrated here for blood pressure under a simulated intervention.

Finally, the intervention experiment is a controlled proof of concept rather than evidence of causal treatment-effect estimation from observational data. Broader external validation, uncertainty assessment, and prospective evaluation remain necessary before clinical use.

capability_assessments.rationale: History-conditioned continuous latent trajectory forecasting across arbitrary horizons on irregular EHRs (L1), with controlled synthetic CFG intervention proof-of-concept.

limitations: EHRs reflect coding practices, missingness, and informative observation times not explicitly modeled.
CFG intervention experiment is a controlled synthetic proof of concept rather than causal treatment-effect estimation from observational data.
No prospective clinical evaluation or uncertainty calibration deployment.
notes: All 32 physical PDF pages extracted/read; Figure 2 (p. 3) and Tables 1-2 (p. 7) visually inspected via rendered PNGs.

legacy_cells.B: Learning Continuous Patient Trajectories from Electronic Health Records
legacy_cells.C: Estévez, Silas Ruhrberg, Liu, Kara, Chiu, Christopher, Owusu, Benjamin Atta, Kadam, Umesh, Altman, Russ B., et al.
legacy_cells.O: Heart failure in CPRD; multiple synthetic disease trajectories (anthracycline exposure, rheumatoid arthritis on DMARD, chronic kidney disease, RRMS, heart failure); general longitudinal EHR records in AMC-EHR and CPRD
legacy_cells.S: Given a patient’s observed EHR history, what clinical events or codes are forecast at a requested future horizon?
legacy_cells.T: Synthetic benchmarks: five cohorts of 20,000 patients each, plus 23,072 Synthea patients; CPRD heart-failure cohort of 868,691 patients; AMC-EHR patients with at least five events (647,447 included)
legacy_cells.X: F2 EHR / ICU event & latent patient dynamics
legacy_cells.AI: Structured longitudinal EHR event records (clinical codes, event sources, continuous measurements, timestamps/time gaps, action and terminal-event indicators)
legacy_cells.AJ: Day-state VAE encoder/decoder: one-hidden-layer MLPs with SiLU and dropout; separate single-layer GRU history encoder (hidden size 128)
legacy_cells.AL: VAE reconstruction cross-entropy for source/code plus 0.1× continuous-block MSE and KL weight 10^-3; history GRU pretrained with next-event cross-entropy
legacy_cells.AS: Latent dimension 64 on synthetic datasets and AMC-EHR; 256 on CPRD
legacy_cells.AT: No filtering update demonstrated; the anchor is encoded from the latest day-state and preceding history is separately summarized by the GRU
legacy_cells.AX: Zero-context ablation reduced average synthetic top-5 accuracy from 0.899 to 0.868 (GP-CFM) and from 0.897 to 0.869 (MMFM).
legacy_cells.AZ: Synthetic latent-state recovery evaluated by fitting a linear readout from encoded anchor states to simulator disease severity; forecast-state MSE reported.
legacy_cells.BD: Treatment assignment (antihypertensive prescription versus suppressed prescription); first prescription defines treatment. The treatment arm is represented by a 32-dimensional embedding.
legacy_cells.BL: Daily day-state event bins; forecast horizons 90, 180, 365, 730, and 1,095 days, with off-grid tests at 45 and 1,460 days; inference integration uses 16 Euler-midpoint steps.
legacy_cells.BS: Decoded source and clinical-code logits plus continuous-valued event features from the forecast latent state
legacy_cells.BT: Decoder outputs source logits, code logits, and a continuous-feature block; primary evaluation is future clinical-code prediction.
legacy_cells.BV: Multi-marginal flow-matching velocity MSE plus decoded one-step endpoint reconstruction loss; VAE reconstruction plus KL loss; history encoder next-event cross-entropy.
legacy_cells.CD: 1,460 days (off-grid horizon; trained horizons extend to 1,095 days)
legacy_cells.CX: Controlled Synthea simulation with known simulator-defined antihypertensive effect; paired and split-arm estimates compared with ground truth. Guided-effect error was 0.07–2.07 mmHg.
legacy_cells.DN: Five controlled synthetic datasets (Anthracycline, RA on DMARD, CKD, RRMS, Heart failure); Synthea; CPRD Aurum/Gold; AMC-EHR
legacy_cells.DQ: Five synthetic cohorts × 20,000 patients; Synthea 23,072 patients; CPRD 868,691 patients (Aurum 815,092; Gold 53,599); AMC-EHR 647,447 patients
legacy_cells.DY: Across real-world datasets, horizon-averaged top-5 accuracy: CPRD EHRFlow GP-CFM 0.638 ± 0.009 vs GP-CFM 0.554 ± 0.021; AMC-EHR EHRFlow MMFM 0.302 ± 0.016 vs MMFM 0.279 ± 0.004. Reported across 90–1,095-day horizons.
legacy_cells.EB: In controlled Synthea hypertension simulation, conditional guidance approximated the simulator-defined −20.48 mmHg effect; reported errors ranged 0.07–2.07 mmHg across variants and paired/split-arm designs.
legacy_cells.EG: Synthetic runs used 0.18–0.76 hours for EHRFlow versus 10.02–56.94 hours for autoregressive baselines; main experiments used one NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada 48-GB GPU and two AMD EPYC 7713 CPUs.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared with decoder-only and encoder–decoder autoregressive transformers, GRU-ODE-Bayes, and Neural CDE. On CPRD, EHRFlow GP-CFM top-5 accuracy was 0.638 ± 0.009; decoder-only was 0.368 ± 0.012.
legacy_cells.EJ: Compared with history-independent flow baselines: CPRD top-5 accuracy was 0.638 ± 0.009 for EHRFlow GP-CFM versus 0.554 ± 0.021 for GP-CFM; AMC-EHR was 0.302 ± 0.016 for EHRFlow MMFM versus 0.279 ± 0.004 for MMFM.
legacy_cells.EK: Ablations tested parameter matching, zeroed history context, end-to-end versus staged training, decoder-loss removal, history-as-source variants, adjacent CFM with history, and history-window length.
legacy_cells.EL: Performance gains depend on metric and horizon: autoregressive models can achieve higher short-horizon macro-AUROC on AMC-EHR; history-conditioning gains are less consistent on Heart failure and Synthea. Authors also note informative observation times are not explicitly captured.
legacy_cells.EO: AMC-EHR is described as de-identified; CPRD data were obtained under licence.
legacy_cells.ER: CPRD study approved through CPRD Research Data Governance (protocol 23 002943); Stanford describes the de-identified STARR-OMOP analysis as pre-IRB, non-human-subject data accessible without IRB approval.
legacy_cells.FB: State is a VAE-encoded continuous latent representation of structured EHR day-states; a separate GRU summarizes the 32 most recent day-states, and the continuous vector field conditions on current latent state, path time, calendar duration, and history context.
legacy_cells.FL: Structured EHR day-state → VAE latent state plus GRU history summary → continuous history- and duration-conditioned flow-matching vector field → decoder for source/code logits and continuous event features; no planner.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces EHRFlow, a history-conditioned multi-marginal flow-matching framework for continuous latent-state forecasting from irregular longitudinal EHRs; evaluates forecasting, external generalization, history conditioning, and a controlled treatment-guidance simulation.
legacy_cells.FN: EHRFlow improves horizon-averaged top-5 clinical-code accuracy over history-independent flow baselines on CPRD (0.638 vs 0.554, GP-CFM) and AMC-EHR (0.302 vs 0.279, MMFM). In a controlled intervention simulation, guidance error was 0.07–2.07 mmHg.
legacy_cells.FO: Authors state EHRs reflect coding practices, missingness, and informative observation times that the model does not explicitly capture; evaluation is limited to continuous and discrete clinical variables; metric/horizon effects vary; intervention experiment is a controlled proof of concept, not causal treatment-effect estimation from observational data; broader external validation, uncertainty assessment, and prospective evaluation remain necessary.
legacy_cells.FP: Authors call for broader external validation, uncertainty assessment, and prospective evaluation; they also suggest testing the latent embeddings as reusable representations for downstream clinical tasks.
legacy_cells.FQ: Existing autoregressive EHR models condition on patient histories but represent events discretely; multi-marginal flow matching uses multiple observations for training paths but does not itself give learned dynamics access to preceding patient history.
legacy_cells.FR: The controlled, simulator-grounded antihypertensive experiment does not establish causal treatment-effect identification from observational EHR data; no planning/control results or prospective patient benefit are demonstrated.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M4 Action service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M6 Rollout service; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Pass the paper’s specified action and time context explicitly into the state-transition interface; preserve the boundary between predictive action sensitivity and identified intervention effects.
legacy_cells.FX: Complete 32-page extracted PDF text inspected (form-feeds as page boundaries): title/abstract p. 1; introduction pp. 1–2; formulation/methods pp. 3–5; experiment setup and main results pp. 6–9; related work/theory pp. 10–18; extended results and tables pp. 19–26; synthetic/real data, implementation, treatment-effect details, compute, and LLM-use appendix pp. 27–32. Relevant tables 1–4, 5–8, and 9–10 inspected along with methods, results, limitations, and conclusion. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: The primary methods and main tables are readable; some dense appendix tables have fragmented column alignment in the extracted text, so ambiguous entries were not used. Demonstrated capability is L2: the treatment-guided test is a controlled simulator experiment, not causal identification or clinical evidence from observational data. No planning, prospective evaluation, or clinical deployment is shown. A:I left untouched; FV:FZ not included.
